name: Consulting English
lede: Learn the language you need to turn messy client problems into clear findings, honest recommendations, and decisions the client actually owns — without sounding like a slide deck.
outcome: The words for framing a problem, defending a finding, and keeping a client conversation honest when the answer is unwelcome.
outcomes: Frame a messy client problem as a question you can actually answer with evidence.
Present a finding so the client hears the implication, not just the analysis.
Push back on a weak assumption without losing the room or the relationship.

aside.title: For the deck you have to defend on Monday.
aside.body: These are the words that keep analysis honest and clients in the room. Use them to explain your thinking, not to hide it.

words.definition: A single stream of related work inside a larger project.
words.example: The pricing workstream reports into the steering committee on Thursday.

words.definition: To pause and review where things stand before deciding.
words.example: Let’s take stock before we commit to the next phase.

words.definition: The factor that most strongly causes a result or trend.
words.example: Cost pressure is the key driver behind the client’s reorganisation.

words.definition: A conclusion you reach after analysing data or interviews.
words.example: Our main finding is that churn starts in the first month.

words.definition: A specific action you advise the client to take.
words.example: My recommendation is to pilot the change in one region.

words.definition: A paid consulting project with a defined client and goal.
words.example: This engagement runs for twelve weeks, with two partners involved.

words.definition: The current level of performance, used for later comparison.
words.example: We need a baseline before we can claim any improvement.

words.definition: A standard or peer result you compare performance against.
words.example: Their delivery cost is well above the industry benchmark.

words.definition: A testable guess about what is causing a problem.
words.example: Our working hypothesis is that pricing, not service, drives churn.

words.definition: The underlying reason a problem keeps happening, not just a symptom.
words.example: We traced the delays to a root cause: approvals nobody owned.

words.definition: A small change that delivers visible results fast.
words.example: Cancelling the weekly status deck is a quick win everyone supports.

words.definition: The full set of steps that create and deliver a product.
words.example: We mapped the value chain to find where margin leaks.

words.definition: A detailed examination of one topic or area.
words.example: Let’s do a deep dive on supply costs next week.

words.definition: A combined view built from several separate sources.
words.example: The synthesis of interviews and data points to one theme.

words.definition: The practical consequence of a finding for the client.
words.example: The implication is that the current model cannot scale.

words.definition: A sequenced plan showing what happens, and in what order.
words.example: The roadmap puts the operating model change in year two.

words.definition: A defined piece of work launched to achieve a goal.
words.example: The cost initiative saved more than the client expected.

words.definition: How a company organises people, process, and technology to deliver.
words.example: Their operating model has three approval layers for every purchase.

words.definition: Any point where a customer or colleague interacts with the business.
words.example: Every touchpoint from booking to billing feels inconsistent.

words.definition: The senior group that meets to oversee a project.
words.example: Take the decision to steerco; the team cannot approve it.

words.definition: The act of raising an issue to someone more senior.
words.example: Without escalation, this decision will sit for another month.

words.definition: A running list of project risks, owners, and mitigations.
words.example: The risk register now has twelve open items, four of them serious.

words.definition: Something you treat as true without proving it yet.
words.example: That forecast rests on one assumption we haven’t tested.

words.definition: How much a result moves when one input changes.
words.example: A quick sensitivity shows the plan breaks at ten per cent.

words.definition: To check a conclusion against several independent sources.
words.example: We triangulated the survey results with the sales data.

words.definition: Built from detailed parts upward rather than set from the top.
words.example: The bottom-up forecast is far lower than the board’s plan.

words.definition: Set from an overall target and then broken into parts.
words.example: A top-down target only works if the teams believe it.

words.definition: Available or visible from the very start of an engagement.
words.example: The client wants a day-one answer on the cost question.
